title: Fever-Dream overtime game posts record WNBA cable viewership
dek: An overtime game between the Indiana Fever and Atlanta Dream on ESPN drew 2.6 million average viewers and peaked at 4 million, the most-watched WNBA game on cable in history. Caitlin Clark scored 26 points and nine assists in the Fever's 95-91 win on August 17.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The viewership figure of 2.6 million average viewers represents a 178 percent increase from ESPN's average regular-season WNBA viewership last year.
bottom_line: The Fever-Dream overtime viewership reset the ceiling for single-game WNBA cable audiences, and ESPN's season-long uptick suggests the market has shifted. Watch whether Indiana and Atlanta's playoff positioning holds steady, as a first-round matchup between them could test whether this audience sustains or was incident-specific.
body: An overtime game between the Indiana Fever and Atlanta Dream on ESPN drew 2.6 million average viewers and peaked at 4 million on August 17, according to an ESPN announcement on August 19. The 95-91 Fever victory marked the most-watched WNBA game on cable in history, regular season or postseason combined.
Caitlin Clark posted 26 points and nine assists in the Fever's win. Angel Reese recorded her 23rd double-double for the Dream despite the loss. The season series between the teams stands even at 2-2.

The 2.6 million average viewership represents a 178 percent increase from ESPN's average regular-season WNBA viewership last year. The broader context shows sustained momentum: through 25 games, WNBA programming on ESPN networks is averaging 1.4 million viewers, up 16 percent compared to the same point last season. Previously, a Fever-Chicago Sky matchup on August 8 on ABC averaged 2.6 million viewers, which was the network's most-watched WNBA game of the season before this overtime contest surpassed it in peak viewers.

Industry measurement firm Nielsen reports that 52 percent of the U.S. population expresses interest in women's sports. Minutes of women's sports watched totaled 46 billion in 2025 and 28.3 billion in the first half of 2026, according to reporting in Awful Announcing.

The teams will not meet again in the regular season but are positioned for a potential first-round playoff matchup. Indiana holds the No. 4 seed with a 23-12 record, while Atlanta occupies the No. 5 seed at 21-13.
